articles.title: 9 Best Tranexamic Acid Serums of 2026 | NBC Selected
articles.summary: Tranexamic acid serum is good for melasma and dark spots. Dermatologists recommend tranexamic acid serum from brands like SkinMedica, Glow Recipe and Paula’s Choice.
articles.body: Dark spots, whether caused by acne, scars or another skin concern, are not only annoying, but also hard to get rid of. Fortunately, a lesser-known ingredient called tranexamic acid, known for brightening skin and fading dark spots and melasma (a type of pigmentation), may come in handy. Tranexamic acid is available to take orally via a prescription or as a topical in over-the-counter serums. Experts I spoke to say the oral version is much more potent, but also comes with more side effects. Serums, on the other hand, are a great way to safely test this ingredient to see if it works for your dark spots, experts say. I asked three board-certified dermatologists to explain exactly what tranexamic acid is and share their favorite tranexamic acid serums. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. What is tranexamic acid? Tranexamic acid is a skin care ingredient derived from the amino acid lysine that can reduce the appearance of dark spots, says Dr. Brendan Camp, a board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology in New York City. “It is considered a skin brightening agent,” she says. As mentioned, you can get oral tranexamic acid prescribed, but it’s also available in over-the-counter serums that address dark spots and melasma. Serums with a high concentration of tranexamic acid (usually between 2% and 5%) in a serum may improve its delivery to skin cells and efficacy, says Camp. The best tranexamic acid serums of 2026 Best for brightening This Glow Recipe serum combines vitamin C and guava extract to brighten your complexion and tranexamic and ferulic acids to soothe redness and irritation, according to Glow Recipe. “I like that it’s a fast-absorbing gel, [which] means it doesn’t feel sticky on skin,” says Camp. You can apply the serum daily, though the brand suggests using it three to four times a week if you have sensitive skin. Best for dark spots Made specifically to address dark spots, this serum from Paula's Choice has 3% tranexamic acid. It also has bakuchiol, a plant-based retinol alternative that can also help with discoloration, says Camp. The serum works for all skin types and can also address dullness and an uneven skin tone, according to the brand. Best for dullness This Inkey List serum combines vitamin C and 2% tranexamic acid to address dark spots and brighten your overall complexion. The gel formula is super concentrated, so a little goes a long way, according to the brand. You can use it morning or night and should apply it after washing your face but before moisturizer and sunscreen. It has a 4.4-star average rating from 439 reviews on Amazon. Best budget pick This budget-friendly serum from Good Molecules combines 3% tranexamic acid with 4% niacinamide, a form of vitamin B known to fade dark spots and brighten your overall complexion, according to the brand. It has a dropper applicator, so you can easily apply a few drops to your fingertips and pat it on your skin after cleansing your face. Best lightweight formula This SkinCeuticals serum comes recommended by Dr. Anne Truitt, a board-certified dermatologist in San Diego, who says this is one of her favorite serums to address discoloration and prevent dark spots. In addition to 3% tranexamic acid, it has kojic acid and niacinamide, both of which also help even out dark spots, according to SkinCeuticals. The formula is very thin, so it spreads easily, and a little goes a long way, according to the brand. Best splurge pick This Skinmedica serum is another favorite of Camp. “This powerful brightening treatment contains a proprietary combination of lotus sprout extract, tranexamic acid and niacinamide to correct the appearance of dark spots and melasma,” she says. You can also use it as a preventative treatment to mitigate future discoloration, according to the brand. The brand recommends using the serum both in the morning and at night. If you use it in the morning, just apply sunscreen afterward as it can make your skin more sun sensitive, according to Skinmedica. Best spot treatment This Murad serum has glycolic acid, which gently exfoliates to address dullness. You can use this serum as a spot treatment and apply it directly to dark spots, or use it all over your face to help even out your skin tone. If you use it in the morning, just apply SPF afterward. Highest concentration of tranexamic acid A little goes a long way with this serum — it has one of the highest concentrations of tranexamic acid on this list. Use just a pea-sized amount on your entire face to address dark spots and even out tone and texture, according to the brand. For maximum results, you can use it morning and night until you see a difference. Best for sensitive skin This Minimalist serum not only helps address acne scars and dark spots, but it also has mandelic acid to gently exfoliate skin, according to the brand. It’s free of fragrance, silicone and sulfates, making it a good option for those with sensitive skin. How I picked the best tranexamic acid serums When shopping for a tranexamic acid serum, dermatologists recommend thinking about these factors, all of which I kept in mind to compile our list: Concentration: Serums have varying concentrations of tranexamic acid in them. It likely won’t be effective if you pick something with a super low concentration. “Look for something that contains between 2% and 5% of this ingredient,” says Camp.Formulation: Most serums with tranexamic acid have other ingredients, too. Choose a serum that has other beneficial ingredients, including antioxidants (like vitamin E and niacinamide), hydrators (like hyaluronic acid and glycerin) or skin-soothing agents (like aloe), says Dr. Anna Chacon, a board-certified dermatologist in Miami, Florida. Rating: Recommendations can help you sift through the many serums available. I included tranexamic acid serums recommended by dermatologists or with at least a 4-star average rating from at least 300 reviews. What are the benefits of tranexamic acid? “Topical tranexamic acid is considered a first-line treatment for mild melasma,” says Truitt. Melasma is characterized by brown splotches on the face caused by the sun or hormonal changes. But tranexamic acid serum can help with more than just melasma. If you have uneven skin tone or hyperpigmentation, the brightening capabilities of tranexamic acid serum may help, says Chacon. “It also has anti-inflammatory benefits and can help calm and soothe skin, which makes it beneficial for individuals with sensitive or reactive skin.” Meet our dermatology experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts with specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. articles.title: Jackson, Mississippi, hanging: Person of interest questioned in Tasia Fortune death
articles.summary: A 29-year-old Black woman from Mississippi was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home in Jackson last week.
articles.body: A 29-year-old Black woman from Mississippi was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home in Jackson last week. The body was discovered Aug. 3 in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance, the Jackson Police Department said in a statement. The Hinds County Coroner’s Office identified the woman as Tasia Fortune. Police said the circumstances surrounding her death remain under investigation. “This is an active and ongoing investigation,” the police department said. “We will provide updates as new details develop.” Detectives say Terence Anderson, 65, was interviewed in Fortune’s death, according to NBC affiliate WLBT. He was taken into custody on an unrelated weapons charge. Anderson’s brother, Tony Anderson, confirmed the arrest to NBC News. He said Fortune and his brother have a 5-year-old son together and that the child lived with Terence. He also said he does not think his brother was involved in Fortune’s death. “Sometimes they’ll have a few occasions where they may get into it or whatever, but that was about it,” Tony Anderson said. “They had their good days, their bad days, but I don’t think he done nothing like that. The autopsy will tell actually what happened to her.” Christy Spivey, Fortune’s mother, told ABC News that she last saw her daughter July 26 at a family reunion in Kentucky. “This has just devastated us,” she said, remembering her daughter as someone who “was strong-minded” and “full of laughs and love.” Spivey said that the last time she saw her daughter she seemed to be in good spirits. “She was better than I had seen her in a long time,” she told the station. “She was at peace.” Spivey said she does not believe Fortune died by suicide. “She did not do this to herself,” she said. “I know my daughter and she did not do this to herself.” Spivey could not immediately be reached for comment Monday. The State Medical Examiner’s Office said it will conduct an autopsy and release its findings once the investigation is complete. Fortune’s death has left some people searching for answers. Ward 3 City Council member Kenneth Stokes said in a letter to U.S. Attorney Baxter Kruger that the city was in “dire need of assistance” while the case is investigated, WLBT reported. During a recent court appearance, detectives said Terence Anderson had been interviewed about Fortune’s death, the news station reported. He denied any involvement but told police that he had an argument with Fortune, according to WLBT. Tony Anderson told NBC News his brother is a convicted felon but had been out of trouble for years and has a job working as a painter. “He pretty much looked after his little boy and worked,” he said. Tony also said Fortune had a substance abuse problem and was living at the abandoned home where her body was found. Jackson police did not immediately respond to a request for comment. articles.title: Thurrock data centre could harm rare bees, says Essex charity
articles.summary: Incredibly rare habitats would be destroyed, the Essex Wildlife Trust warns.
articles.body:
Plans to build a new data centre could threaten the habitat of one of Britain's most endangered plants and a rare species of bumblebee, a wildlife trust said.

A planning application has already been submitted for the Google data centre at Arena Essex Raceway in Thurrock, which is designated as a local wildlife site.

It is home to the rare broad-leaved cudweed and shrill carder bumblebee and the Essex Wildlife Trust fears "incredibly rare" habitats would be "destroyed".

A Google spokesperson said it took "our environmental responsibilities very seriously".

Data centres are giant warehouses full of powerful computers used to run digital services, such as movie streaming, online banking and artificial intelligence.

There are 568 data centres listed in the UK, according to the data centre map.

Emily Buttress, from the Essex Wildlife Trust, said her team was worried about the water and energy usage required, the warming effect on the surrounding land, and a lack of research about the long-term impacts of these buildings.

"We are quite worried with the rapid development of data centres," she said.

"What would it do for the local community in a water drought county? We are not against development, but it has to happen sustainably."

The Arena Essex Raceway announced in 2018 that it would stop hosting speedway fixtures for the Lakeside Hammers team.

Meanwhile, the Essex Wildlife Trust says the surrounding grassland and woodland has become home to 687 invertebrate and 439 plant species.

The trust said this included dingy skipper, which is a small moth-like butterfly, and the shrill carder bumblebee, which was only found in two areas in England.

It was designated as a local wildlife site in 2006. This does not offer legal protection from development, but it means council planners expect developers to look after the ecology.

Nightingale birds, the brown-banded carder bee and the five-banded weevil-wasp have also been recorded at the site.

But Global Infrastructure UK Limited bought the 129-acre (52-hectare) site in July 2023 for £47m (exclusive of VAT).

It submitted plans for the data centre on behalf of Google last year, and as part of the application, consultancy firm Mallory Land Ltd said the proposals took into account the ecology there.

In a statement submitted as part of the plans, Mallory Land Ltd said: "The demand for data centres has expanded significantly in recent years, driven by exponential growth in digital services, the emergence of artificial intelligence, cloud-based technologies, and the increasing adoption of smart infrastructure."

Google said data centres were vital to the UK economy and for online services.

"We share the Essex Wildlife Trust and Buglife's view that development at the former Arena Essex site must be sustainable," a spokesperson said.

"Our goal is to regenerate the site, bringing long-term investment and jobs to Thurrock while taking our environmental responsibilities very seriously."

The company had worked closely with Natural England and ecologists, they added, to "guarantee a 10% biodiversity net gain", "as well as ensuring a substantial part of the site is preserved for new public open space, green links, retained habitat, and the long-term enhancement of key woodland corridors".

articles.title: Trump critica Suprema Corte após revés no voto pelo correio | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão mantém os procedimentos adotados pelos estados para o voto pelo correio; Trump critica ministros indicados por ele que votaram contra a medida.
articles.summary: Trump critica Suprema Corte e ataca juízes indicados por ele após a manutenção das regras de voto pelo correio nas eleições dos EUA.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com repórteres antes de embarcar no Air Force One na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, em Maryland, em 9 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Foto de BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP

A Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos rejeitou a tentativa do presidente Donald Trump de restringir o voto pelo correio nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato, encerrando uma série de medidas judiciais de última hora enquanto a votação já está em andamento.

A decisão permite que os estados continuem enviando cédulas pelo correio seguindo os mesmos procedimentos adotados há anos. Quase um terço dos eleitores americanos vota dessa maneira.

Trump criticou os ministros em uma longa publicação nas redes sociais nesta terça-feira (15), e afirmou: “Essas não são as pessoas que entrevistei”.

“A incapacidade e a falta de vontade da Corte de fazer a coisa certa pelo nosso país ficarão registradas, de forma muito negativa, nos anais da História”, escreveu Trump.

“Esta Suprema Corte é intimidada e pressionada pela Esquerda Radical a tomar decisões que fizeram os Estados Unidos retrocederem pelo menos cem anos”, afirmou.

Os ministros Neil Gorsuch, Amy Coney Barrett e Brett Kavanaugh foram indicados por Trump durante seu primeiro mandato, mas votaram contra o presidente na decisão de segunda-feira (14).

“Essas não são as pessoas que entrevistei para servir na Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos. São apenas uma sombra do que eram originalmente”, disse Trump.

O presidente também afirmou que a Corte está custando “trilhões de dólares aos Estados Unidos” por causa de decisões “absurdamente ruins”, de uma magnitude que tornaria difícil para o país “se recuperar ou se curar”.

Caixa do Serviço Postal dos EUA instalada em Manhattan, em Nova York — Foto: Andrew Kelly/Reuters

Incerteza era maior onde voto pelo correio é predominante

Eleitores da Califórnia, Colorado, Havaí, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Vermont e Washington votam quase inteiramente pelo correio. Esses estados não têm uma ampla rede de locais de votação presenciais.

“A decisão dá aos eleitores e aos responsáveis pelas eleições a segurança de que precisam antes de uma eleição federal importante. Ela também envia uma mensagem clara ao país: presidentes não conduzem eleições, as pessoas conduzem”, afirmou Tobias Read, secretário de Estado do Oregon e membro do Partido Democrata.

Cisco Aguilar, secretário de Estado de Nevada, disse que sua reação à decisão da Suprema Corte foi de “alívio, mas também de entusiasmo, porque hoje os eleitores realmente venceram em toda a América”.

Mais da metade dos eleitores de Nevada votou pelo correio nas eleições primárias de junho. Segundo Aguilar, “parte do estrago já foi feita” por causa de alegações falsas que afetaram a confiança das pessoas no voto pelo correio.

“Vocês podem confiar no processo”, afirmou Aguilar aos eleitores. “Por favor, participem.”

articles.title: Atibaia: Moradores andam de barco e perdem móveis após chuva | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradores do Jardim Kanimar estão tendo que se deslocar por barcos da Defesa Civil da cidade.
articles.summary: Moradores do Jardim Kanimar estão tendo que se deslocar por barcos da Defesa Civil da cidade.
articles.body:
As chuvas que atingiram Atibaia nos últimos dias causaram diversos estragos na cidade, principalmente para os moradores do bairro Jardim Kanimar. Imagens de drone mostram o algamento nas ruas da cidade (veja vídeo acima)

Nesta terça-feira (15), a situação ainda era complicada para os moradores. Em entrevista ao vivo ao Link Vanguarda , o caminhoneiro Antônio Pestana disse que perdeu móveis com a água.

“5h da manhã comecei a fazer limpeza, tirar o barro porque dessa vez veio cheio de barro. Perdemos bastante móvel, está tudo na área para colocar para descarte”, afirmou.

Na Rua João Evangelista Chamadoira, moradores estão tendo que se deslocar por barcos, conduzidos por agentes da Defesa Civil da cidade.

Segundo o balanço da Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo, divulgado na manhã desta terça-feira (15), o acumulado de chuva na cidade foi de 52 milímetros nas últimas 72 horas.

articles.title: Vacinação de cães e gatos em Volta Redonda: doses gratuitas | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa vai acontecer na Praça Brasil, de 9h às 17h. Segundo a prefeitura, serão ofertadas 4 mil doses de vacinas, incluindo a V8 para cães e a V3 para gatos.
articles.summary: Vacinação de cães e gatos em Volta Redonda oferece 4 mil doses das vacinas V8 e V3 gratuitamente na Praça Brasil neste sábado e domingo.
articles.body:
Volta Redonda recebe vacinação gratuita para cães e gatos neste final de semana — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Volta Redonda

Volta Redonda (RJ) vai receber uma ação para a vacinação de cães e gatos neste fim de semana. A iniciativa acontece nos dias 19 e 20 de setembro (sábado e domingo), na Praça Brasil, localizada na Vila Santa Cecília, de 9h às 17h.

Segundo a prefeitura, a iniciativa faz parte do projeto “Rural é Mais Saúde Animal”, da Universidade Federal Rural do Rio de Janeiro (UFRRJ). Os tutores interessados em vacinar seus animais devem se cadastrar no site .

Ainda de acordo com a administração municipal, equipes da universidade estarão no local para vacinar os animais. Ao todo, serão disponibilizadas 4 mil doses de vacinas, incluindo a V8 para cães e V3 para gatos.

A prefeitura informou ainda que para garantir a segurança e o bem-estar dos tutores, animais e os servidores, é recomendado que cães de grande porte sejam levados com focinheira e que os gatos sejam transportados em caixas de transporte.

articles.title: EUA dão milhões em assistência militar a 4 países latino-americanos | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão ocorre após visita de secretário de Estado Marco Rubio a países latino-americanos. Panamá, Peru, Equador e Colômbia passarão a receber verba norte-americana com foco em 'combater o narcoterrorismo em nosso próprio quintal', segundo Washington.
articles.summary: Decisão ocorre após visita de secretário de Estado Marco Rubio a países latino-americanos. Panamá, Peru, Equador e Colômbia passarão a receber verba norte-americana com foco em 'combater o narcoterrorismo em nosso próprio quintal', segundo Washington.
articles.body:
O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, e o presidente da Colômbia, Abelardo de la Espriella, em 8 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Luis Acosta/AFP

O governo Trump retirou dezenas de milhões de dólares em assistência militar estrangeira destinada a países da Europa e do Oriente Médio para passar a apoiar países da América Latina com governos alinhados ideologicamente ao presidente Donald Trump .

O Departamento de Estado notificou o Congresso dos EUA nesta terça-feira (15) sobre a realocação de verbas, um total de US$ 52 milhões (cerca de R$ 267,3 milhões), que passarão a ser entregues aos seguintes países:

Até o momento, esse financiamento militar estrangeiro era destinado a Eslováquia, Macedônia do Norte, Tunísia e Iraque.

O Departamento de Estado afirmou que os recursos serão usados para "combater o narcoterrorismo em nosso próprio quintal e ajudar a continuar garantindo a segurança do Canal do Panamá", acrescentando que o Hemisfério Ocidental foi historicamente negligenciado na assistência militar dos EUA.

"Esses recursos impedirão que adversários estabeleçam posições estratégicas em nosso hemisfério", afirmou o departamento, em uma crítica velada à China, que tem buscado cada vez mais ampliar sua presença na América Latina.

A medida ocorre apenas uma semana após uma visita do secretário de Estado norte-americano, Marco Rubio , à Colômbia, ao Equador e ao Peru. A Colômbia e o Peru elegeram governo conservadores recentemente: Abelardo de la Espriella e Keiko Fujimori, respectivamente.

Durante sua visita oficial, Rubio prometeu apoio adicional a esses países, o que vai em linha com a política externa do 2º mandato do governo Trump, que prioriza o domínio do Hemisfério Ocidental com ênfase no combate ao tráfico de drogas e à imigração ilegal.

O financiamento militar estrangeiro fornece aos países beneficiários recursos dos contribuintes norte-americanos para que possam comprar equipamentos militares de empresas de Defesa dos Estados Unidos .

Ainda não estava claro, até a última atualização desta reportagem, qual fatia dos US$ 52 milhões que cada país latino-americano receberia.

A transferência dos recursos não elimina o financiamento militar estrangeiro destinado à Tunísia, ao Iraque, à Macedônia do Norte ou à Eslováquia , embora o valor exato que permanecerá disponível para esses países não estivesse imediatamente claro.

O Departamento de Estado afirmou, porém, que a atual distribuição do financiamento "não está alinhada com a prioridade dada pelo governo" ao Hemisfério Ocidental.

articles.title: Humanidade perderá autonomia sem limite no avanço da IA, diz Nobel | G1
articles.standfirst: Vencedora do Nobel da Paz, Maria Ressa afirma que sistemas cada vez mais autônomos podem reduzir a capacidade de decisão das pessoas e defende regras urgentes para limitar o avanço da tecnologia.
articles.summary: Vencedora do Nobel da Paz, Maria Ressa afirma que sistemas autônomos podem reduzir a capacidade de decisão das pessoas e defende regras urgentes para limitar tecnologia.
articles.body:
Maria Ressa, ganhadora do Prêmio Nobel da Paz — Foto: Gwladys Fouche/Reuters

A inteligência artificial pode reduzir a autonomia da humanidade se não forem aprovadas leis para limitar seu avanço , afirmou Maria Ressa, ganhadora do Prêmio Nobel da Paz.

A jornalista filipino-americana, vencedora do Nobel da Paz de 2021 em reconhecimento, entre outros fatores, ao seu trabalho sobre o poder das grandes empresas de tecnologia, atua como copresidente do painel científico internacional da ONU sobre IA . O grupo estuda como a tecnologia está transformando a vida das pessoas em todo o mundo.

Segundo Ressa, a tecnologia já capturou a atenção das pessoas por meio das redes sociais e depois passou a explorar a necessidade humana de conexão e intimidade. Ela defende que os cidadãos pressionem políticos e autoridades para aprovar regras que regulamentem o uso da inteligência artificial .

“Pedir regulamentação não é uma questão de liberdade de expressão. É uma questão de segurança pública”, disse Ressa, que também é cofundadora e presidente-executiva do site de notícias Rappler, à Reuters.

“Acho que estamos naquele momento em que, se isso não acontecer, vamos perder o controle. A situação ficará fora do nosso alcance se não agirmos agora”, afirmou durante uma visita a Oslo, onde participou de uma conferência sobre ameaças às democracias.

“A inteligência artificial não é nem artificial nem inteligente. Ela existe há cerca de 70 anos, e já passou por três ondas que chegaram ao grande público”, disse.

Segundo Ressa, a primeira fase foi marcada pelas redes sociais, que capturaram a atenção dos usuários, aprofundaram a polarização e contribuíram para o isolamento das pessoas.

“A segunda fase consistiu em 'hackear' nossa biologia, novamente por meio da intimidade, com os chatbots”, disse Ressa. “A terceira envolve a chamada IA agentiva e multiagentiva, com modelos avançados capazes não apenas de simular comportamentos humanos, mas também de agir em nosso lugar.”

Alguns críticos, entre eles o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, rejeitam os apelos por maior regulamentação da IA por temer que isso prejudique a disputa tecnológica com a China. Ressa classificou esse argumento como uma “boa manobra de relações públicas”.

“Na verdade, a China estabelece mais salvaguardas para seus cidadãos do que o Vale do Silício para o restante do mundo. Se você usa o TikTok, a versão disponível na China tem restrições de idade”, disse.

Antes mesmo de Dario Amodei, presidente-executivo da Anthropic, defender uma desaceleração no avanço dos modelos de IA diante dos crescentes temores de uso indevido da tecnologia, Ressa já sustentava que o primeiro passo para promover mudanças é responsabilizar as big techs.

“O primeiro passo é fazer com que as empresas sejam responsabilizadas pelos danos que causaram”, disse. Ela elogiou as ações judiciais nos EUA que levaram a Meta a pagar até US$ 18 bilhões ao longo da próxima década e a restringir fortemente o uso do Facebook e do Instagram por adolescentes.

Ela elogiou as medidas adotadas pela União Europeia e por países como a Austrália para estabelecer limites de idade nas redes sociais, mas afirmou que isso não resolve a “falha fundamental” de que as ferramentas desenvolvidas pelas empresas de tecnologia também causam dependência entre adultos.

“Sabemos que isso é prejudicial. Portanto, vocês deveriam remover os recursos que geram dependência, não apenas para adolescentes, mas para todos nós”, disse. “Não são apenas os jovens que estão sendo manipulados politicamente ao redor do mundo.”

Segundo Ressa, devem ser criadas plataformas de comunicação desenvolvidas por grupos de interesse público e fora do controle das grandes empresas de tecnologia, da mesma forma que governos investem em bens públicos, como parques e praças. Ela citou como exemplo o lançamento do Rappler Communities, em 2023.

Baseado no protocolo aberto, seguro e descentralizado Matrix, o Rappler Communities permitiu que a redação do Rappler se conectasse diretamente aos leitores e que os próprios leitores interagissem entre si para, nas palavras de Ressa, “ter conversas reais”.

O Rappler convidou outros veículos de comunicação das Filipinas a participar da iniciativa e agora está expandindo o modelo para outros países do Sudeste Asiático.

“É um lugar onde as pessoas podem se sentir seguras no ambiente digital, onde podem conversar umas com as outras e, mais importante ainda, ouvir umas às outras para que a grande obra da democracia se concretize”, afirmou.

articles.title: Cícero Lucena quer revogar PPP da Cagepa e descentralizar saúde na PB | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do MDB ao governo da Paraíba participou de rodada de entrevistas no JPB1, das TVs Cabo Branco e Paraíba, nesta terça-feira (15).
articles.summary: Cícero Lucena, candidato ao governo da Paraíba, detalha planos para revogar a PPP da Cagepa e descentralizar serviços de saúde, em entrevista ao JPB1.
articles.body:
O candidato do MDB ao governo da Paraíba, Cícero Lucena, afirmou nesta terça-feira (15), em entrevista ao JPB1, das TVs Cabo Branco e Paraíba , disse que vai revogar a Parceria Público-Privada (PPP) da Cagepa por não considerar viável esse mecanismo para o esgotamento sanitário no estado. Ele também disse que pretende descentralizar os serviços de saúde de cidades como João Pessoa e Campina Grande.

"Nós vamos ter que revogar, porque esse projeto de R$ 3 bilhões é investimento em 25 anos, o Marco do Saneamento é para agora é 2033, então faltam 8 anos, sete anos (...) o que quero lhe dizer é que esse projeto não está pensando nisso. O investimento que está previsto nesse projeto para João Pessoa é 25% do que João Pessoa precisa. Então nós temos que revogar e encontrar mecanismos", disse Cícero.

As promessas foram feitas em entrevista para as TVs Cabo Branco e Paraíba , em rodada de sabatinas com os candidatos ao governo do estado iniciadas nesta semana. As entrevistas serão realizadas nos dias 14, 15 e 16 de setembro, com duração de 30 minutos, entre 12h10 e 12h40. Participarão desse formato os candidatos de partidos com mais de cinco representantes no Congresso Nacional. A ordem definida por sorteio foi :

Sobre a descentralização da saúde, Cícero Lucena diz que pretende fazer que com isso os serviços possam ser prestados com maior eficiência. Ele citou um exemplo de João Pessoa, onde foi prefeito, em que a cidade, conforme dados apresentados por ele, recebe um grande número de pessoas vindas de outros locais.

"O que estamos vendo nesse governo? A centralização e sobrecarregando as duas principais cidades do estado, João Pessoa e Campina Grande. João Pessoa tem cerca de 850 mil habitantes, tem 150 mil que tem plano de saúde, era pra João Pessoa atender 700 mil cartões SUS, em números redondos, atende 1,4 milhões de cartões SUS. São pessoas do interior do estado, que por ausência, por omissão do governo, deixa de ser atendido no interior e vêm em busca da opção. É o ser humano que a gente tem que atender", disse.

Cícero Lucena, candidato ao governo da Paraíba, diz que vai revogar PPP da Cagepa em entrevista para as TVs Cabo Branco e Paraíba — Foto: Gustavo Demétrio/g1 PB

Um dos temas abordados pelo candidato Cícero Lucena foi que o Ministério Público Eleitoral propôs a impugnação da candidatura dele por uma suposta proximidade com uma facção criminosa em João Pessoa. A Justiça Eleitoral não acatou esse pedido e o candidato pôde concorrer.

"Eu tenho uma tranquilidade em relação a isso. Quantos candidatos têm processo no Brasil? (...) Qual a minha responsabilidade em crescer a facção? Responsabilidade era do governo. Esse cidadão que entrou com ação contra mim devia ter entrado contra a candidatura do governador, que é o responsável. Por exemplo, diz que tem um centro de monitoramento em João Pessoa e chega em Cabedelo, quais são as câmeras que estão lá?", disse.

Sobre a impugnação da candidatura da filha dele, Janine Lucena, para a primeira suplência de senador, ele disse que a retirada posterior dela da candidatura foi conversada para evitar desgaste pessoal no que ele diz ser "um processo de muita injustiça".

"Minha filha tem passado por um processo de muita injustiça. não seria justo a gente continuar oferecendo ela para que em momento eleitoral as pessoas que não querem disputar o voto pela conquista praticar algo que fazer ela sofrer e consequentemente todos nós sofrer com a injustiça que ela passa", contou.

No que diz respeito a substituição de Janine Lucena por Matheus Lucena, irmão dela, para concorrer na vaga para a primeira suplência, Cícero disse que isso foi conversado com a candidatura principal ao senado, de Veneziano Vital.

"Pela representação, pelo convite de Veneziano, por considerar que a representação de João Pessoa na chapa do senado como suplente é um fator de construção de proposta e de integração do estado", explicou.

Valorização das forças de segurança e equilíbrio financeiro

O candidato também respondeu pergunta sobre a valorização das forças de segurança no estado, caso seja eleito governador. Ele citou exemplos de quando era prefeito de João Pessoa para dizer que vai realizar valorização dos policiais no estado.

"Eu não estou fazendo promessa de campanha, te dou testemunho de vida. Dois exemplos agora na gestão de prefeito, os agentes da Guarda Municipal Metropolitana era um dos piores salários da região, hoje, estamos no top-10, e mais, um agente da Guarda Municipal, hoje, se aposenta com o salário igual ao capitão da Polícia Militar. É prática de gestão, a minha história, minha vida, eu aprendi a cuidar dos servidores, para que eles me ajudam na minha missão", disse.

Ele ressaltou que esse tipo de postura não passa necessariamente somente por questões salariais, mas também por recursos humanos relacionados a tudo isso.

"Não devemos tratar especificamente só de salários, mas do conjunto da segurança (...) nós temos que tratar dos recurso humanos da segurança é algo fundamental para você conquistar aquilo que a população espera e merece", explicou.

Sobre equilíbrio financeiro, Cícero Lucena respondeu novamente citando João Pessoa como exemplo, isso porque, na visão dele, enquanto prefeito não deixou de lado serviços, "qualidade de vida" e investimentos.

"A prefeitura de João Pessoa é um exemplo disso. Nós avançamos serviços, qualidade de vida da cidade, investimentos e tudo que praticamos. Somos (nota) AA no Tesouro Nacional (...) Você tem capacidade gerencial para isso, o estado vai ser equilibrado, agora vai ter prioridade, o que é que vai precisar fazer? Nós temos que ter a análise crítica e a capacidade de fazer essa análise e graças a Deus, Deus me permitiu isso, eu já tive muitas experiências na vida", disse.

Sobre a relação de um eventual governo de Cícero Lucena na Paraíba, o candidato falou que pretende utilizar a Universidade Estadual da Paraíba (UEPB) como "instrumento" para um programa de desenvolvimento.

"E vamos, sim, cumprir o que a lei determina, a autonomia pedagócia-administrativa, e também a financeira com a UEPB, porque a UEPB vai ser instrumento do desenvolvimento do estado. Vou sentar com a UEPB para que ela seja a responsável pelas escolas técnicas profissionalizantes do nosso estado", ressaltou.

O candidato citou ainda como exemplo quando ele foi governador do estado, em 1994, após a renúncia de Ronaldo Cunha Lima. Ele diz que naquela época já pensava sobre questões relacionadas com a universidade.

"A UEPB foi criada pelo município de Campina Grande, depois estadualizada. Quando eu fui governo junto com Ronaldo Cunha Lima, nós adotamos a política da descentralização da UEPB, é tanto que eu como governador criei o campus de João Pessoa, que antes já tínhamos criado um no interior. Aqui, na época com dois cursos, ciências da computação e gestão pública. Eu já pensava nisso em 1994", disse.

articles.title: Mulher é amarrada e morta com marteladas na Grande Fortaleza | G1
articles.standfirst: Rose Garcia, de 29 anos, foi assassinada depois de ser amarrada dentro da própria casa, na cidade de Caucaia, na manhã desta segunda-feira (14). Suspeito ainda não foi detido.
articles.summary: Rose Garcia, de 29 anos, foi assassinada depois de ser amarrada dentro da própria casa, na cidade de Caucaia, na manhã desta segunda-feira (14). Suspeito ainda não foi detido.
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 29 anos foi assassinada após levar golpes com um martelo dentro de casa, na manhã desta segunda-feira (14), no município de Caucaia , na região metropolitana de Fortaleza. O ex-companheiro da vítima é suspeito de ter entrado na residência dela e amarrado o pai dela antes de cometer o crime . A polícia investiga o caso como feminicídio.

A vítima foi identificada como Rose Garcia, que morava no bairro Lagoa do Barro. Ao g1 , uma amiga de Rose, que preferiu não ter a identidade revelada, detalhou que a dona de casa tinha um filho de 7 anos com o ex-companheiro, de quem estava separada há cerca de quatro anos.

Conforme o relato de amigos e familiares, Rose havia saído para deixar o filho na escola e depois teria ido para a academia durante a manhã. Ao chegar em casa, ela teria encontrado o suspeito dentro da residência mantendo o pai dela amarrado.

O pai da vítima teria conseguido fugir e não teve ferimentos, mas a dona de casa foi amordaçada e assassinada pelo suspeito. O corpo dela encontrado dentro da residência, onde ela morava com o pai, o filho e um irmão.

Rose Garcia foi morta com marteladas em Caucaia, na Grande Fortaleza, e ex-companheiro é suspeito — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo apuração da TV Verdes Mares, o irmão de Rose tinha ido ao trabalho e não estava em casa no momento do crime.

A identidade do suspeito não foi divulgada oficialmente pela polícia. Conforme o relato de familiares e amigos de Rose, o homem dizia não aceitar o fim do relacionamento com a ex-companheira.

“Nesses quatro anos em que ficou separada, ela não se envolveu com ninguém. Ela costumava ir para a igreja, ia para festa de aniversário de criança, fazia tudo com a família”, relatou ao g1 a amiga da vítima.

Ainda de acordo com ela, Rose não contou para as pessoas próximas se havia sofrido agressão ou ameaças do ex-companheiro.

O caso está sendo investigado como feminicídio pelo Departamento de Homicídios e Proteção à Pessoa da Região Metropolitana, em Caucaia. Conforme a Secretaria da Segurança Pública e Defesa Social (SSPDS), o suspeito do crime já foi identificado. Ninguém foi preso até o momento.

Rose Garcia, de 29 anos, foi morta após levar golpes com um martelo nesta segunda-feira (14), em Caucaia — Foto: Reprodução

Conforme apuração da TV Verdes Mares, o ex-companheiro de Rose foi visto passando de motocilcleta perto do local onde ela estava sendo velada , na manhã desta terça-feira (15). Familiares e amigos prestaram homenagens à vítima em uma igreja evangélica frequentada por ela, no bairro Lagoa do Barro.

Algumas das pessoas que estavam no velório comunicaram o que viram à polícia e passaram a circular de carro pela região, com a expectativa de localizar o suspeito. No entanto, o ex-companheiro de Rose não foi encontrado até o momento.

O corpo de Rose Garcia deve ser sepultado no município de Caucaia na tarde desta terça-feira (15).

articles.title: 'Tareekh Pe Tareekh': 100% complete, still no keys - Inside RERA’s extension loop
articles.summary: India News: A housing project misses its promised completion date. The developer asks for more time. The regulator grants it. There is nothing extraordinary about.
articles.body: A housing project misses its promised completion date. The developer asks for more time. The regulator grants it. There is nothing extraordinary about that sequence. Construction can be held up for many reasons, some of them outside a developer's control. Sometimes a few more months are exactly what a project needs to get buyers their homes. The difficulty begins when the wait becomes tareekh pe tareekh.The question is simple. When a delayed project is given more time, how often does that extra time actually result in completion? There is no national public number that answers it.TOI tried to get closer to one by examining Maharashtra, one of the country's largest RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority) markets. It analysed 4,237 registrations appearing on MahaRERA's list of projects kept in abeyance after their completion dates had lapsed, as the list stood on Sept 10, 2026. A public reconstruction of MahaRERA filings by ReraGenie was used to identify projects with recorded extension histories. TOI then checked all 110 that the reconstruction showed with at least three recorded extension-history events against MahaRERA's own records.The reconstruction identified 1,154 of the 4,237, or 27.2%, with at least one recorded extension-history event. There were 392 with two or more and 110 with three or more. The 27.2% is not a failure rate. These projects were already on a lapse-related abeyance list, and abeyance is an administrative status. MahaRERA says projects on its lapse-related abeyance list have their bank accounts frozen, while promoters are prohibited from executing agreements for sale or sale deeds until the required compliances are fulfilled.Not every extension-history event represents a new deadline either. More than one filing can relate to the same revised date. What the exercise does establish is how often the completion clock can keep running long after the original date has passed.Abhay Upadhyay, president of the Forum for People's Collective Efforts (FPCE), a homebuyers' body that has examined the use of extensions across several states, argues that the statute is not where the problem lies. He says, "RERA is watertight, what has gone wrong is the practice built around it." The force majeure route under Section 6, in his view, has come to be treated almost as a given, with promoters approaching the regulator confident that an extension will follow.When the percentage does not tell the whole storyOften numbers can flatter to deceive. Take Indraprasthanagari Phase 1 in Pune. MahaRERA was told in one extension filing that the project was 98% complete. In another it was 95%. In a later filing it was back to 98%, while the revised completion date moved from December 2022 to May 2023 and then June 2024. An engineer's certificate in January 2023 put the project cost at ₹16.62 crore, with ₹1.66 crore still to be spent. An architect's certificate from the same period put key finishing and services work at 80% in Building A and 90% in Buildings B and C; the same figures appeared a year later.The same gap between a headline completion number and the documents underneath it appears in FPCE's 192-page report on project extensions. The report describes its cases as samples, not a census.In one Karnataka project, an April 2024 regulatory order recorded the project as 94% complete. A later order cited completion at 76%, relying on progress information that was more than two years old.Upadhyay's objection is to the sequence. "As soon as a promoter wants an extension, they should be asked the hard question, in the first instance only," he says. In Uttar Pradesh, he says, the report found instances where UPRERA granted extensions and carried out site visits afterwards.The project that was 97% complete in 2020Gajanan Plaza in Mumbai's Borivali shows how long the gap between "almost complete" and delivery can stretch. In January 2020, its promoter told MahaRERA that 97% of the project had been completed onsite. Some buyers had been promised possession as far back as 2012.They had originally booked residential flats before the project was converted to commercial use. By July 2024, 11 complainants across seven units, who had paid a combined ₹1.67 crore, were still before MahaRERA seeking enforcement of orders in their favour.In one proceeding, the regulator recorded "intentional default" in complying with its earlier directions. Gajanan Plaza had originally been registered to finish on Dec 31, 2018. At a February 2025 hearing, the promoter sought time until December 2027, saying Phase 1 was almost complete but financially dependent on a proposed Phase 2.MahaRERA's live project page, as of September 2026, carries a revised completion date of April 30, 2028. The page states that the date includes the four-month extension granted under MahaRERA Order 66/2026, a blanket force majeure extension applied automatically to eligible projects across the state.Extensions are a large part of the systemMahaRERA's own annual figures give a sense of how much of its work is now extension work. In 2025-26, the regulator reported 4,204 fresh registrations, 2,488 corrections and 3,687 timeline extensions. That works out to nearly 88 extensions for every 100 fresh registrations. Extensions made up 35.5% of those three categories. That does not mean 88% of new projects were delayed. An extension granted in 2025-26 can relate to a project registered several years earlier.But the figures do indicate how much regulatory activity now involves projects whose original timelines have already changed. Keeping a registration alive can also matter commercially. In four of the 110 projects examined by TOI, promoters explicitly stated that an extension or extension number was needed to continue selling unsold flats.When 100% still isn't possessionAmong the 110 projects, TOI found at least 12 where a promoter filing described the project or overall construction as at least 95% complete while seeking more time. At least five explicitly claimed 100% completion. At least four made a 95%-plus claim in more than one filing.Shiv Sparsh Phase II is a case in point. Its promoter described the project as 100% complete in three extension filings while also stating that fire and lift NOCs were awaited. The revised deadlines eventually ran through July 2024. A March 2025 architect's certificate again put the main building-work categories at 100%. Its separate common-area entry for "Fire Protection & Fire Safety requirements" carried no completion percentage. At other projects, even the basic progress update may be missing. In May 2026, MahaRERA issued show-cause notices to 8,212 of 33,029 registered housing projects after they failed to file mandatory quarterly progress reports for the January-March quarter by the April 20 deadline.What happens when another deadline is needed?TOI also examined 10 MahaRERA orders issued in 2025 under Section 7(3), which allows the authority, instead of revoking a project's registration, to let it continue subject to conditions. All 10 recorded that the promoter had failed to obtain the 51% majority allottee consent referred to in MahaRERA's procedure. All 10 nevertheless granted further time. That is not, in itself, improper. Across the orders, though, the argument is substantially the same: refusing continuation could stop the project and harm buyers, and the "balance of convenience" therefore favours allowing it to proceed subject to conditions.Upadhyay says the pattern is not confined to Maharashtra. Extensions granted despite the absence of the 51% consent also turn up in FPCE's examination of orders across states.The law allows more than one routeThe Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act was passed in 2016 and came fully into force on May 1, 2017, after years of demands for a law to discipline a sector in which buyers had little recourse against delay. It is a central statute administered locally: each state and union territory frames its own rules and appoints its own authority. MahaRERA, which began work in 2017, is among the oldest and busiest.RERA does not contain a simple one-extension rule. Section 6 limits extensions granted under it to one year in aggregate. Section 7(3), separately, allows a regulator, instead of revoking registration, to keep it in force subject to conditions. MahaRERA has used this route in post-lapse continuation proceedings.In its 2017 Neelkamal Realtors judgment, the Bombay High Court held that continuation beyond the ordinary extension framework could be considered case by case in exceptional, compelling circumstances. For buyers, another clock runs alongside the regulatory one. Under Section 18, an allottee who stays in a delayed project is entitled to interest for every month of delay until possession. A buyer who withdraws can seek a refund with interest. Upadhyay points to Supreme Court rulings affirming that entitlement and says very little has changed on the ground.The database which is neededEven official estimates put the scale of housing stress high. A government-appointed committee headed by Amitabh Kant cited Indian Banks' Association estimates of around 4.12 lakh stressed dwelling units involving ₹4.08 lakh crore in legacy stalled projects. FPCE reaches a much larger figure: ₹12.44 lakh crore affecting around 27.6 lakh families, by its estimate. The figure is modelled, not a project-by-project count.India does have a count of registered RERA projects. When the Centre launched its Unified RERA Portal in September 2025, 1,51,113 projects had been registered nationally. At the same meeting, however, the government said a nationwide project database should still be prepared.And in March 2026, the housing ministry told Parliament that detailed state-level information sought by MPs was "not centrally maintained". However a publicly accessible national record linking the complete journey of a project is currently missing. Upadhyay says the gap is not for want of asking. The issue has been raised in central forums and instructions to furnish the data have been issued, he says, but the data has not followed.Section 8, which allows a project to be taken out of a promoter's hands, should be used far more often, Upadhyay argues, on the reasoning that the prospect of losing the project is what makes a developer move. By the time a project has lost its financial viability, action against the promoter achieves little. "What a RERA registration ought to carry is a definitive guarantee to the ordinary buyer," Upadhyay says.Ten years after RERA came into force, the unresolved question is no longer whether delayed projects sometimes need more time. It is how regulators decide when more time is still a solution, and when it has simply become another deadline.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Scotland fans allowed to buy alcohol at upcoming games
articles.summary: Trial alcohol sales took place earlier in the year for the national team's friendly games.
articles.body:
Scotland fans will be able to buy alcohol at upcoming games at Hampden Park following a "good result" in earlier trials.

A ban is usually in place in Scottish football but trial alcohol sales have been taking place recently , including for the national team's friendlies against Japan and Curaçao earlier this year.

Those fixtures saw alcohol served from pop-up hospitality bars in the stadium concourse.

Four occasional licences to cover two areas of the stadium concourse have now been approved for the games against Switzerland on 29 September and Slovenia next month.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Addressing the city's licensing board on Friday, licensing lawyer Stephen McGowan said: "You granted essentially equivalent licences for the friendlies… I'm very pleased to say they both went well, there were no adverse incidents.

"I think it was a good result for everyone involved with Hampden."

The bars will open at 17:45 ahead of the 19:45 kick off. Alcohol sales will stop at 19:00 with supporters allowed 15 minutes to drink up.

The hospitality areas will be in the level five east bronze and level five west bronze concourses. Only fans with tickets for seats in these areas are able to access the bars.

McGowan said the games would be the "the next step in this wider project", gathering further data.

He said the project is taking an "incremental" and "prudent" approach and "public safety has been at the heart of that process", adding: "You've now got the comfort of knowing that two matches have been licensed without any difficulties."

The general sale of alcohol has been prohibited in Scottish football stadiums since 1981.

articles.title: China built a 120-metre tower above a waste plant; visitors can now climb it to look over a facility processing 8,000 tonnes of rubbish a day
articles.summary: Rest of World News: China has turned a huge part of a waste treatment facility in Guangzhou into a public attraction. A former chimney at the Fushan Circular Economy Indu.
articles.body: China has turned a huge part of a waste treatment facility in Guangzhou into a public attraction. A former chimney at the Fushan Circular Economy Industrial Park has been transformed into a 120-metre-high tower, allowing visitors to look across the site from above. The facility processes thousands of tonnes of household waste every day and has become a popular tourist attraction. This development shows how waste treatment is shifting in China, with rubbish increasingly being processed for energy and material recovery instead of simply being buried.The 120-metre tower overlooking an 8,000-tonne waste plantThe tower stands at the Fushan Circular Economy Industrial Park in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province. The State Council Information Office reports that the former chimney was converted into a 120-metre-high tower.Xinhua reported that the facility has been developed with a garden-like setting. Visitors can climb the tower, enjoy coffee and take in a panoramic view of the site. The location has also become part of a national 3A-level tourist attraction.The setting gives an unique public face to an operation that normally remains out of sight. Beneath the tower, the facility deals with 8,000 tonnes of household waste every day, making it one of the large-scale waste treatment sites serving the city.China is moving towards a different way of treating wasteThe Guangzhou facility forms part of a wider change in China's approach to household rubbish. Xinhua reported that the country has been moving away from relying on landfill and towards methods that can recover energy and useful materials from waste.The scale of urban rubbish has made that change increasingly important. Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen each generate more than 20,000 tonnes of household waste a day, according to Xinhua. In earlier years, large quantities of rubbish accumulated in landfills around some cities.The shift means waste is increasingly treated as a material that can still provide value after it has been discarded. Incineration has become a major part of that system, with modern plants using the heat produced during burning to generate electricity and, in some cases, supply heat or steam to industry.What happens when household waste is incineratedAccording to Xinhua, most of China's household waste is now incinerated instead of simply buried. Modern facilities can use the heat generated during the process to produce electricity, while some also supply heat to nearby industrial users.Foshan, also in Guangdong, provides one example. Its eco-industrial park processes 4,500 tonnes of household waste each day. The high-temperature steam produced during treatment is supplied through pipelines to nearby factories, where it replaces fossil fuels.The process is also designed to control harmful emissions. Xinhua reports that modern incinerators operate their furnaces at temperatures above 850 degrees Celsius, allowing dioxins to be broken down. Activated carbon, bag filters and other systems are then used to deal with substances remaining in the flue gas.Shanghai's Laogang Waste Disposal Base provides another example. Xinhua says much of its operation, including unloading, fermentation, incineration and emissions monitoring, is automated. Its flue-gas pollutants are described as being near zero, with the facility performing beyond Chinese national and European Union standards.Turning waste ash into useful materialWaste treatment does not end with incineration. The material left behind can also be processed and reused. Xinhua reports that bottom ash accounts for about 20% of the waste and contains materials such as iron, copper, aluminium and small quantities of gold and silver.At the Fushan Circular Economy Industrial Park, ash produced in 2025 was processed into material for environmentally friendly bricks used in roads and buildings. The quantity processed was about 600,000 tonnes.The figures also show how quickly incineration has expanded in China. Official data cited by Xinhua states that incineration accounted for 78.1 per cent of China's urban household waste treatment capacity by November 2025. That was 19.2% points higher than at the end of 2020.What happened to China’s old waste mountainsThe move towards modern treatment can also be seen in what is happening to former landfill sites. Xinhua reports that more than 80% of Chinese cities had completed the remediation of ageing waste mountains by 2025.Shenzhen provides a notable example. The city's former Yulong landfill operated from 1983 to 1997 and contained 2.55 million cubic metres of waste. The site was later capped, but urban development eventually surrounded the landfill with high-rise buildings.In 2024, China began its largest landfill excavation project at the site. About 6,000 tonnes of waste are excavated each day. Light combustible materials, including plastic and rubber, are sent to nearby incinerators for power generation.Once the work is complete, the former landfill is expected to provide about 300,000 square metres for a digital industry cluster and an ecological green valley.According to Xinhua, China's waste treatment sector is expected to move further towards resource recovery during the 2026–2030 period. For visitors to Fushan, that transition can now be seen from 120 metres above the ground. What was once simply a chimney has become a viewing tower over a working waste facility, offering a unique perspective on one of the less visible parts of urban life.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Telford amphitheatre attracts thousands after summer reopening
articles.summary: The venue in Telford Town Park reopened in July for the first time since the 1990s.
articles.body:
More than 7,800 people visited Telford's recently restored lakeside amphitheatre over the summer.

The 400-seat venue reopened in July for the first time since the 1990s and put on a range of theatre, comedy, family shows and free band days.

Earlier in the summer it went through a six-week refit, including the replacement of the stage, which sits at the waters edge.

Angela McClements, the Telford and Wrekin councillor responsible for culture, tourism and leisure, said it had been a "fantastic first season for the amphitheatre".

She also said the interest in events there "shows exactly why this venue means so much to the residents of Telford and Wrekin".

The summer season concluded with a performance of Shakespeare's Macbeth on 3 September and the council said planning had begun for next summer's events.

The amphitheatre is made up of a 400-seat terraced bowl with bench-seats, leading down to a wooden stage beside a pool.

In its heyday, during the 1980s, the amphitheatre by Randlay Pool in the park was "a vibrant cultural hub" which hosted regular live gigs and performances, before later closing in the 1990s, the council said.

Residents approached the authority about restoring the feature in 2024 and funding was approved earlier this year for work to be carried out.

New lights, stage, security rails and electrics have been installed as well the site being tidied up.

articles.title: Second seabird in Herefordshire blown 100 miles off course
articles.summary: Vet Elliot Goodwin thinks the bird is likely to have come from Skomer Island in Wales.
articles.body:
A Manx shearwater has become the second seabird in a year to be found in Herefordshire after apparently being blown about 109 miles (175km) off course from the Welsh coast.

Its arrival comes a year after a puffin, also thought to have come from Skomer Island, was found in a garden near Stoke Lacy.

Elliot Goodwin, from Vets for Pets in Hereford, described the Manx shearwater as a "remarkable species".

He said the bird's "highly unusual" appearance in the county was likely caused by inexperience and strong south-westerly winds.

He said the bird was most likely a juvenile that had taken a wrong turn after leaving its nesting burrow and had probably come from Skomer Island, which is home to a large breeding colony.

Goodwin said the species was capable of journeys of about 6,000 miles during migration to South America.

Although Herefordshire is a relatively short trip for a bird capable of travelling thousands of miles, he said Manx shearwaters were adapted to life at sea and were not well equipped to navigate trees and buildings.

"They make use of the wind that skips across the surface of the sea," he explained. "They tire very quickly over land."

Unlike Oona the puffin, the unnamed Manx shearwater was uninjured and was returned to the Welsh coast after becoming lost.

articles.title: Number of people claiming key disability benefit hits record high
articles.summary: An ongoing review into Personal Independence Payments (Pip) has found the system is "not fit for purpose".
articles.body:
The number of people claiming Personal Independence Payments (Pip) in England and Wales has hit a record high, according to new government figures.

As of July, just over four million people were entitled to claim the benefit, compared to 3.83 million the previous year, an increase of 7%, data from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) showed.

Pip is designed to support people with the extra costs of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions, and eligibility is not affected by a person's income or savings.

In July, Sir Stephen Timms, who is leading a review on Pip, said in his interim report that the system was "not fit for purpose".

Of the 4.1 million claimants, those aged 50 and above accounted for more than half.

Just under three in ten were aged 30 to 49, while 17% of claimants were aged 16 to 29.

Pip seeks to offset the extra costs that can occur for those living with certain long-term health conditions.

According to the charity Scope, the extra cost of being disabled – known as the disability price tag – has reached more than £1,100 a month.

The DWP said the increase in the Pip caseload had actually "slowed", falling from a rise of 400,000 in the 12 months to July 2024, to 260,000 in the 12 months to July 2026.

But they agreed the system was "no longer fit for purpose", adding that the Timms review's recommendations would "lay the foundation for sustainable reform".

But Helen Whatly, shadow work and pensions secretary, said Labour was "too quick to write people off and too slow to help them into work" - adding that it was "costing us a fortune".

Pip has been in the spotlight since the summer of 2025 when the government, led by former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer, proposed reforming and tightening eligibility criteria for the benefit as the cost of running the system increased.

Spending on Pip stood at £16.3bn in 2019-20, when adjusted for inflation to today's prices, and had increased to £27.3bn by 2024-25, government figures showed.

It is currently forecast to rise to £41.5bn by 2030-31.

Reform proposes £50bn welfare bill cut with changes to disability payments for millions

Disability benefit not fit for purpose, minister leading review says

How a rise in ADHD benefits claims is adding to welfare spending challenge

But dozens of Labour MPs expressed concerns about the plans and, fearing its own members would vote down the reforms, the government U-turned.

Instead, it commissioned a review into Pip led by Sir Stephen, the minister for social security and disability, to make recommendations that would make it "fit and fair for the future".

The interim report published in the summer said the system had become a barrier to work for many, and the process of applying for it was found to be "dehumanising".

Under the current assessment system, a health professional scores claimants on everyday tasks such as washing, getting dressed and preparing food using a zero to 12 scale.

Earlier this month, the review's "emerging recommendations" suggested more face-to-face assessments would take place, and while cash payments would remain the foundation, there would also be non-cash support available.

The Timms review is expected to be published in full later this year.

articles.title: Jennifer Hollowell Watkins was last seen on camera on June 26, 2025, in Washington, North Carolina | Dateline
articles.summary: 45-year-old mother of three Jennifer Watkins was last seen in Washington, North Carolina in June 2025. The Beaufort County Sheriff’s Office is investigating.
articles.body: If there’s one thing Amber Hollowell Trimpe knows how to do, it’s advocating on behalf of someone else. The North Carolina native works as a health advocate for people experiencing domestic violence. But in June 2025, Amber’s work became personal when her sister, Jennifer Hollowell Watkins, went missing from Washington, North Carolina. Since then, Amber has become her sister’s advocate in the family’s search for answers. “Jenny was bubbly and bright and laughed and had this huge imagination,” Amber said. “She was super talented, super creative.” Jennifer had worked for the North Carolina Estuarium, an environmental education center, in Washington, North Carolina, near where she and Amber had grown up in Blounts Creek. “We spent a lot of time out in nature learning; my dad taught us flora and fauna, how to respect the land,” Amber remembered. “Working at the estuary was her way that she applied all those things we had learned as a kid.” According to Amber, Jennifer suffered a major back injury around 2017, left her job after that, and transitioned to life as a full-time mom to her three sons. “Her boys were her lifeblood,” Amber said. “Everything in her life was about her boys. That’s what she was most proud of.” According to Amber, at the time of her disappearance, Jennifer had custody of her youngest son, and a domestic violence protective order (DVPO) was in place against the child’s father, Samuel Foster. Amber says that on the night of June 24, Foster went to the residence where Jennifer lived with a roommate, and Jennifer reached out to her former stepmother, Janet Windley, for assistance. Dateline spoke with Janet Windley who said that when Jennifer called her that night she, in turn, called the Beaufort County Sheriff’s Office (BCSO), and went to Jennifer’s residence. According to Janet, deputies arrived at the scene and arrested Foster. Janet described herself as a confidante of Jennifer’s and said it was normal for her to watch Jennifer’s youngest son for short periods of time. She offered to babysit the child because Jennifer was upset. According to Janet, Jennifer accepted her offer and left the residence with Samuel Foster’s cousin, Sarah Waller, saying they were going to the beach to look for jobs. “She needed a change of surroundings,” Janet said. Janet said she then brought Jennifer’s son back to her home to look after him, with the understanding that Jennifer would call when she returned. Jennifer never called. Around 10:00 p.m. on June 26, Jennifer was seen on security cameras at a Speedway gas station on the west side of Washington. “That’s the last time she’s pictured on camera,” Amber said. Janet told Dateline that by the morning of June 29, Jennifer still hadn’t returned, so she reported her missing to the BCSO. BCSO provided Dateline with the incident report, which confirms that Janet reported Jennifer missing that day and told officers about Jennifer’s plans to travel to the beach with Waller on June 24. According to the incident report, BCSO issued a be-on-the-lookout alert (BOLO) for Jennifer and pinged her cell phone. Its last ping was in the area of VOA Road on June 26. BCSO could not get an updated location because the phone had been turned off. Investigators made contact with Waller, who told them she was last with Jennifer on June 27, 2025. According to the incident report, Waller said she was sleeping in her vehicle, parked at the end of Ponderosa Road off VOA Road in Washington, when a man named Bobby Nixon approached and woke her. Waller said that was when she realized Jennifer was no longer there and that she did not know where Jennifer had gone. According to the incident report, investigators spoke with Nixon, who said that when he observed Waller’s car parked on Ponderosa Road, the passenger door was wide open. The incident report does not state Nixon’s connection to Jennifer, but he told investigators he had not seen her since June 24. According to the incident report, Samuel Foster contacted the sheriff’s office and said he heard Jennifer was missing and wanted his son. When asked if he had seen Jennifer, Foster told investigators he had just been released from jail and had not seen her. Investigators searched Foster’s property and “could not locate Jennifer or anything out of the ordinary,” the report states. Dateline contacted the Beaufort County Sheriff’s Office for further details, but has not yet received a response. Dateline left voicemails for both Samuel Foster and Sarah Waller seeking comment. Foster has not responded. Waller responded by text saying, “Do not call this # again.” The Beaufort County Sheriff’s Office has not named any persons of interest or suspects in Jennifer’s case. Amber asks anyone with information on what happened to Jennifer to come forward. “It doesn’t really matter if -- how minuscule a detail. If it’s something that happened leading up to those final days in June of 2025, come forward with it,” Amber said. “Because we don’t know what -- what speck of information might be the bridge we need.” On December 22, 2025, Beaufort County Crime Stoppers announced a $10,000 reward “for information that leads to solving this case.” For Amber, finding answers is especially important for Jennifer’s sons. “I want to be able to give them answers. I want to be able to give justice to my sister,” she said. “I don’t want them to question where their mother is.” Jennifer would be 46 years old today. She is 5 ‘1”, and weighed 115 lbs., at the time of her disappearance, with shoulder-length brown hair and blonde highlights. She has two large birthmarks, one on her right shoulder and another on the back of her left thigh. If you have any information regarding Jennifer’s disappearance, please contact Beaufort County Crime Stoppers at 252-974-6400 or submit your confidential tip online at If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic abuse, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 or visit for more resources. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.
